headlines.title: Looking back on Dolly Parton's groundbreaking career and music legacy
headlines.description: Country music legend Dolly Parton has died at the age of 80. Her family announced the news in a video posted to social media. NBC News' Chloe Melas reports on the icon's life and legacy.

headlines.title: Canada announces new tariffs on the U.S. as trade tensions rise
headlines.description: The Canadian government retaliated against President Donald Trump’s latest wave of tariffs by raising tariffs on steel products and imposing a swath of new duties on $20 billion in U.S. products exported to Canada. NBC News' Christine Romans reports on the new tariffs unveiled by Canada as the trade war with the U.S. continues.

headlines.title: Canada Prepares to Retaliate on Trump's 50% Tariffs
headlines.description: After President Donald Trump imposed 50% tariffs on some Canadian goods, Canada is saying it has leverage. “We have what the world wants,” Prime Minister Mark Carney said. Meanwhile, Trump’s pressure campaign on Iran is underway with what he calls “economic D-Day,” slapping fresh sanctions on 60 foreign entities and threatening to cut off countries unless they stop doing business with Iran. NBC’s Gabe Gutierrez reports for TODAY.

headlines.title: Lindsay Clancy murder trial in Massachusetts: Day 20
headlines.description: Watch live coverage as the murder trial of Lindsay Clancy, who is accused of killing her three young children, continues in Massachusetts after the defense rested its case.

headlines.title: Gen Z’s Analog Summer Filled With Throwback Tech and Hobbies
headlines.description: Despite all of the technology at their fingertips, it appears a lot of younger people are choosing more hands-on hobbies synonymous with their parents and even grandparents, from needlepoint to birdwatching. NBC’s Joe Fryer reports for TODAY on the rising popularity of analog activities.

headlines.title: The Future Is Here: Air Taxis Unveiled in Downtown Los Angeles
headlines.description: An air taxi was unveiled Monday in downtown Los Angeles. Developers plan to put landing sites all over the city and are hoping to have it ready to go in time for the 2028 Olympics, pending FAA approval.

headlines.title: Amazon’s steering wheel-free robotaxi expands to more cities
headlines.description: Amazon's Zoox robotaxis are now hitting the streets in cities like Las Vegas and San Francisco, becoming some of the first self-driving vehicles approved for commercial use without a steering wheel or dashboard. NBC News' Chief Tech correspondent Joanna Stern talks with Tom Llamas about the new cars.

headlines.title: Phone Safety Settings Guide: What to Turn On vs. Keep Off
headlines.description: There are countless safety and privacy settings on our phones and devices so NBC’s business and data correspondent Brian Cheung stops by TODAY to share the best practices for protecting your privacy, including deleting unused apps, turning on multi-factor authentication, shutting off data tracking, and more.

headlines.title: Chinese Humanoid Robots Smash Usain Bolt’s 100-Meter Record
headlines.description: At the World Humanoid Robot Games, a sports competition in China, robots showed they can run faster than humans, with two smashing Usain Bolt’s 100-meter sprint. The display of technological might is also meant to display feats of science. NBC's Janis Mackey Frayer reports for TODAY.

headlines.title: Will People Really Flip Over the New Era of Foldable Phones?
headlines.description: Foldable smartphones are growing in popularity and now Apple is reportedly preparing to launch its own version, so NBC’s Brian Cheung joins TODAY to break down this nostalgic tech trend including the benefits, the downsides, the cost breakdown, and more.

headlines.title: Verb CEO says you should own your data and get paid for it
headlines.description: Companies collect and profit from our personal data every day, but most of that value never makes its way back to consumers. Verb CEO Cyrus Beschloss explains how his company aims to give users control of their information and the ability to earn money from it.

headlines.title: China hosts second Humanoid Robot Games as arms race with U.S. heats up
headlines.description: The second annual World Humanoid Games are set to take place in Beijing. It comes as tension continues to build between China and the U.S. in a technological arms-race. NBC News' Janis Mackey Frayer is there with a preview of some of the up-and-coming robotic talent.
